title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

 age_of_fire : With the dragons defeated, the Lords took over the world, ruling as Gods from their seat of power in the land of Lordran. It was a prosperous era, and many nations were born. In time, however, the First Flame began to fade, and with it the power of the Gods, leading to an era of decay and the emergence of the Undead Curse. If the Flame were to gutter out completely, it would end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark.

title: First Flame
snippet: But then, somewhere in the hollows deep underground, a great and primordial fire that would come to be known as the First Flame burst into being. In doing so, it brought disparities into the world for the first time, such as heat and cold, life and death, and light and dark. Soon, humanoid creatures emerged from the darkness surrounding the First Flame, attracted by the fire. These creatures found sources of power called souls near the Flame, and took on the diverse powers the souls gave them. With the strength of four particularly powerful souls, four figures were born: Gravelord Nito, the Witch of Izalith, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight, and the Furtive Pygmy. Using their newfound power, these Lords and their forces overthrew the ancient dragons, ushering in the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: However, it becomes apparent that at this stage in the Age of Fire, which has been unnaturally prolonged far beyond its intended length, there is little that can be done to keep the First Flame lit. Even if the Ashen One chooses to link the Flame, the fire that results from this rebirth is small and feeble in comparison to the raging inferno that resulted from the Chosen Undead linking the Flame in *Dark Souls*.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Although the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods lasted for centuries, at some point the First Flame began to fade. Gwyn understood that if the Flame went out, the Age of Fire would be succeeded by an Age of Dark, a new order of humans led by a Dark Lord. Fearful of this outcome, the god made a drastic decision: In order to maintain the order of Gods, he would sacrifice himself to link the dying Flame and prolong its life. He trusted none but himself to carry out the sacrifice involved; he thus divided the power of his Lord Soul among the members of his clan and handed down the power of the sun to his children, leaving his firstborn son to inherit his titles. Gwyn also tasked his sons and Frampt with shepherding the humans into following his example, linking the Flame generation after generation, to uphold his Age of Fire, each of them becoming Lords through the process.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

At the end of the game, after defeating the Soul of Cinder, the Ashen One, in case they chose to link the First Flame, is covered from head to toe in a soft-looking fire, unlike the flaming inferno of the first game. The implications are clear: The First Flame itself now is so weak that it cannot be kindled anymore.

The First Flame, as the Age of Fire, is beyond saving.

In *The Ringed City*, it is implied that the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire has caused irrepairable damage to the world, as is shown after Filianore's awakening: the fertile lands seen when the Ashen One arrived in the city are replaced by a seemingly unending, as-far-the-eye-can-see's barren wasteland of unknown nature.

snippet:

Although the meaning of this ending is ambiguous, it likely symbolizes that the Ashen One acquires the power of the First Flame's power for themselves rather than in accordance with any of the great powers at play. The Usurpation of Fire ending also sees the Ashen One acquiring the First Flame rather than link it or let it die, although the absence of the followers of Londor in this ending hints that the Ashen One's plans are their own.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
***Ash Seeketh Embers**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. Before the flames fade, the Ashen One may strike her down. The Ashen One steps over the limp body of the Fire Keeper and takes the First Flame into their own hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the flame, offering it to the Darksign Sun.
***The Usurpation of Fire**: If the Ashen One allowed Yoel to draw out their true strength a sufficient amount of times through the Dark Sigil, followed Yuria's instructions and "married" Anri, the Ashen One may, instead of linking the fire, absorb it into themselves. The Ashen One collapses from the strain and awakens before a Darksign Sun turned white, and also finds Yuria, Anri, and an army of hollows greeting them as their Lord and praying for the Ashen One to make Londor whole.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Following the failure of this first contingency plan, a second plan is activated: Unkindled, those who had previously tried to link the First Flame but who had failed to do so, are resurrected from their graves in the Cemetery of Ash, and tasked with placing the rebellious Lords of Cinder upon their thrones so that the First Flame might be linked once more. The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: First Flame
snippet:
Aware that time was quickly running out for his kingdom, Gwyn and a detachment of his knights entered the Kiln of the First Flame. The knights stood guard as Gwyn sacrificed himself to the waning Flame at the Kiln's centre. This immediately reinvigorated the First Flame, creating a firestorm that turned the Kiln to ash, and incinerated all of Gwyn's knights, creating the Black Knights and dooming them to wander the lands as disembodied spirits forever after.

Gwyn's sacrifice succeeded in perpetuating the Age of Fire for a time, but *Dark Souls* takes place at least 1000 years later, and the Flame is quickly fading once again. Soon, only Dark will remain.

title: Fire Keeper (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
If given the eyes of the first Fire Keeper, she sees a world without fire, and is frightened by the mere thought of it. Even so, she is willing to end the cycle permanently if the Ashen One requests it. If the Ashen One chooses to realize her dream, she will be summoned to the Kiln of the First Flame. At that time, she will hold the First Flame in her hands and let it die out, thus unlocking the End of Fire ending. If the Ashen One chooses to succumb to their desire, and kill her during the ritual; the power of the First Flame would fall to their hands.

The Fire Keeper can also be talked to, and her dialogue changes throughout the course of the game.

She will psychically respond to most gestures performed by the player.

If killed, she will always respawn at Firelink Shrine, stating that as a Fire Keeper, she cannot die.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: At the close of a period in the Age of Fire, The Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame, becoming Lords of Cinder. An indefinite amount of time later, the destined Lord of Cinder Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame, which led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves, to once again serve as kindling for the Flame. The Abyss Watchers refused to once again sacrifice themselves to the Flame, instead returning to Farron Keep, leaving their throne at Firelink Shrine empty.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Gwyn's act of linking the First Flame came to be a point of controversy for several figures; namely Kaathe and Aldia would regard Gwyn's sacrifice as having "unnaturally" extended an Age of Fire that was never meant to last, inhibiting the potential of humans in the process. As of the time of the Chosen Undead, one consequence of Kaathe's actions lies beneath Firelink Shrine: the ruins of New Londo, which was captured by the Darkstalker and had to be flooded before the Abyss within could spread to the surface world.

The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Yhorm refused to serve as fuel for the First Flame a second time due to the fact that, once awakened from his grave, he realized that his sacrifice had been futile. The sorcerers of the Profaned Capital had continued to experiment on the Profaned Flame he had tried to quell with his sacrifice and as a result the entire city was destroyed, making his life of service meaningless even after the end. The moment he rises from the grave, he can be seen already howling in despair. In addition, he may also have simply understood the state of the world, now corrupted beyond any possibility of traditional salvation through the linking of the Fire, and simply decided to await death in the ruins of his city.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even after possibly hundreds of thousands years after the first linking of the Flame, Frampt (or other serpents affiliated with his ideology) continued to propagate the cult of the linking of the Flame; influencing kingdoms, rulers and simple Undead to continue the tradition started by Gwyn. When the First Flame drifted up to position itself on the nascent kingdom of Lothric, Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city too. Over time the serpents passed on the culture of linking the Flame to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to preserve the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Frampt or his kin were represented in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angel wings, showing their central role within the kingdom, considered "divine messengers". title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet:
Sometime before or after linking the Flame, Ludleth was exiled from his country. He then collaborated with Lothric, where he ensured that all Fire Keepers to come would be deprived of their eyes, to prevent them from observing a future without the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness, where the First Flame was all but extinguished.

Ludleth eventually linked the First Flame, taking pride in sacrificing himself of his own volition and convinced that, if in life he had been only a pygmy, in death he would have been celebrated as a true Lord. However, he also seems to express remorse for his actions, asking to be forgiven.

title: Darksign
snippet:
Centuries after this abuse, the First Flame started to naturally fade out, and the Darksign, which used the power of the Flame to contain the Dark Soul, weakened too, leading humans to come back to life as Undead, but also cursing them to eventually become Hollows, as the Darksign would consume their Humanity still forced on their bodies.
Thus, Gwyn sacrificed himself to rekindle the First Flame and forcibly postpone the end of the Age of Fire. Now with a martyr figure to use as powerful propaganda, the Undead Prophecy was spread throughout Lordran to encourage all who bear the Darksign to come to Lordran and claim powerful souls, making them worthy of filling the Lordvessel and succeed Lord Gwyn, rekindling the dying flame and prolonging the Age of Fire. The Chosen Undead would find themselves nearly hollow for several centuries after the rekindling of the First Flame, bearing the cursed mark of the Darksign, the greatest sin against humanity.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Humans
snippet: Over time, others would repeat Gwyn's sacrifice—either for their own reasons or to follow in his footsteps—to rekindle the First Flame. As the First Flame was not intended to burn as long as it had, the fabric of reality began to suffer.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them the Abyss Watchers too rose from their graves, but refused to sacrifice themselves again to link the Fire, choosing to return to their Keep in Farron. However, the Followers were no longer present to cull the warriors that would become corrupted by the Abyss, consequently forcing the Watchers to do so themselves, wasting their strength to kill each other to contain the spreading corruption.

title: Timeline
snippet:
After Yhorm links the First Flame, the court sorcerers continue to experiment with the Profaned Flame
The court sorcerers create gargoyles as guardians and soldiers
The court sorcerers equip the gargoyles with staffs capable of using the Profaned Flame as a weapon
In a ritual, the Profaned Flame goes out of control and devours the city, but only burns the people
Only a family of sorcerers and their handmaidens survive
The Profaned Flame is however stored in the skulls of its victims and used by the survivors
Due to the **Stagnation**, the ruins of the Profaned Capital are submerged underground, drifting all the way beneath the city of Irithyll
The First Flame starts to fade again but Prince Lothric, the designated Lord of Cinder, refuses to link the Flame
Yhorm, as one of the previous Lords of Cinder, is exhumed from his graves to use the embers of the Flame still within him as fuel for it

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

Calling it "futile" is a euphemism: the unnatural prolonging of the First Flame's lifespan came with disastrous, if not, downright catastrophical proportions: when the Lords of Cinder started to resurrect, somehow, portions of their countries and homelands were, literally, "teleported" to Lothric, changing the landscape in unpredictable ways.

By the time *Dark Souls 3* takes place, the damage caused to the world by the unnatural prolonging of the Age of Fire seems to be irreversible.

As the games progresses, the sun itself starts to change, until it eerily resembles the Darksign itself.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

snippet: Now bereft of most of his Lord Soul's power and with only the power of his soul, Gwyn left for the Kiln of the First Flame, the structure built to house and protect it, with only his robes, his mighty greatsword and his powerless crown, accompanied only by a guard of Black Knights. Countless people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual started with Gwyn's sacrifice. All the Fire Keepers who served their purpose of guiding their Champions would be disposed of and dropped inside the Bell Tower of Firelinking Shrine, piling in up in the dozens. Even more were those Champions who tried and failed to link the Flame, becoming the Unkindled, and were buried near the shrine in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard of all those who failed in their task.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: After her father Gwyn linked the First Flame, his throne passed to his firstborn son who, in a betrayal of his father's legacy, chose to ally with the dragons, the ancient enemies of the gods, and was therefore dethroned, exiled and his name eradicated from history. She abandoned Anor Londo along with most other deities and moved to an unknown location. Sometime after her departure she married Flame God Flann.

title: Lothric
snippet: During the founding of Lothric, the First Flame drifted north towards the kingdom, forever marking the history and culture of its people. Due the presence of the Flame, the lands of the world began a geographical and temporal drift towards the city of Lothric, owing to the space-time altering effects of **Convergence.****** One or more Primordial Serpents developed an interest in propagating the cult of Firelinking within Lothric, to uphold the Age of Fire and the tradition started with Gwyn's sacrifice. Eventually Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city. Over time, serpents passed on the Firelinking culture to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to uphold the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Primordial serpents were depicted in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angelic wings, showing their central role within the kingdom and their perception as divine

title: Age of Dark
snippet: of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

snippet: Gwyn derived the bulk of his power and influence from the First Flame, which he shared with the other gods, but in time the Flame began to die. title: Lore
snippet: The Age of Fire began prosperous and rich, but soon the fires started to go out again and with them the power of the Lords. In an effort to prolong Age of Fire, the Witch of Izalith tried to recreate the First Flame, but the experiment failed and a flame called "The Flame of Chaos" is created instead, which transformed her into the Bed of Chaos and many creatures into the demons that roam Lordran. Her children are transformed as well, with her son becoming a flame demon called Ceaseless Discharge and her daughter Quelaag and her sister partially into spiders. Her followers stay loyal to her, however, and become known as the "Witches of Chaos". Only her daughter, Quelana, escaped the fire and becomes the mother of pyromancy. This being said, Mother Izalith did eventually *succeed* in stabilizing the Chaos Flame with 2 of her sisters.

snippet:

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet: The deformed Aldia is encountered several times by the Bearer of the Curse, to whom he imparts his extensive knowledge on the nature of life. He expresses outrage over the actions of the Lord of Light, who cursed humans into mortality and introduced the cycle of light and dark by linking the First Flame. Aldia's bleak worldview considers mankind as "props on the stage of life", persevering merely through obsession. While acknowledging the merits of the Age of Fire, he labels the roots of this "warm, resplendent" world as a lie, with the linking of the Fire as its original sin. Nevertheless, Aldia realizes that one could wish to inherit this order, even if built on a "tender, exquisite" lie. Instead of submission to the peace provided by the status quo, he offers a third "path"; obscure and unpaved, yet could perhaps ascend the scope of Light and Dark.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin at some point learned of Gwyn's existence and his story but not his name, referring to him merely as the "Lord of Light". He understood how Gwyn altered the natural order and began linking the Flame, which extended the Age of Fire against the course of nature, and he expresses his outrage at Gwyn for making men lesser than their original form as the "Lord of Light" banished Dark and all that stemmed from Humanity with the Darksign, defining it as the "First Sin" committed against humans and their nature.

title: Chosen Undead
snippet:
Chosen Undead -  Dark Souls - character - epilogue 
 epilogue : After offering the necessary Lord Souls, the doors to the Kiln of the First Flame are opened to the Chosen Undead. Gwyn, now reduced to a Lord of Cinder, breathes his last breath in the final confrontation with the Chosen Undead. It is here that the Chosen Undead may make their decision of either linking the flame or walking away from it. Depending on which course of action is taken, one of the two possible endings will be unlocked. Whether the player has aligned themselves with Kaathe or Frampt will not affect the ending of the game.

***Link the Fire:** This ending is unlocked if the player rekindles the First Flame. The Chosen Undead offers themselves as kindling to the fire. Sacrificing all of their souls, the Chosen Undead is consumed by the flames and the Age of Fire is extended, as life is breathed into the First Flame once more.

Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

Gwyn's firstborn preserved his father's design and instructions, shepherding humans on the path to the Linking of the First Flame to continue the Age of Fire. In fact, underneath Anor Londo, a city was built exclusively for the undead, with an altar inside for the firstborn of Gwyn, and the aim of guiding a chosen undead who would one day sacrifice themselves to the Flame. Inside the city was the Undead Parish, a church at the center of the cult of the burg and connected to the first test to start on the path of Firelinking and ring the first Bell of Awakening. snippet:

snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.

Black Knight -  Dark Souls - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Black Knights were once the proud Silver Knights of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Long ago they fought chaos demons and were charred black, also giving them high Fire resistance. Many traveled with Lord Gwyn to the Kiln of the First Flame, and were burned to ashes when he linked the First Flame, wandering the world as disembodied spirits ever after. Their disembodied spirits can be seen roaming the stairs descending into the Kiln of the First Flame.

 age_of_deep_sea : The is a condition that the world would assume once the First Flame has gone out.

Originally, it had been expected that the Age of Fire would be followed by an Age of Dark. However, following mankind's oppression under the Darksign since time immemorial, fanned by the unnatural prolongation of the First Flame's life, the Dark Soul and its fragments have been corrupted and stagnated. Determined to free mankind from the shackles of the Gods, the Sable Church of Londor studied the Dark Soul and the Darksign. title: Londor
snippet: roots : The origins of Londor can be traced back to when the Primordial Serpent Kaathe welcomed three human sisters into his service as his maidens: Elfriede, the eldest; Yuria, the middle child; and Liliane, the youngest. Kaathe's past attempts to uncover a Dark Lord, to prevent the linking of the First Flame, and to finally bring about the Age of Dark had largely failed; the order of the old gods remained dominant and the Age of Fire persevered, albeit increasingly faintly. His failures notwithstanding, the Primordial Serpent was steadfast in his pursuit, and eventually enlisted the sisters as his capable hands. And so Kaathe taught the three sisters, already highly skilled fencers, the art of the Dark Hand, used for absorbing the humanity of its victims. In turn, they used their battle prowess to establish **the Sable Church**, an organization that claimed to offer salvation to Hollows. They settled in the land that would become known as Londor, "the Hollow Realm".

At some point, Elfriede, as leader of the Sable Church, departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. snippet: An Angel which likely sprouted from a Londor Pilgrim seems to have triggered a chain of events that led to a war of faith within Lothric. One day, Gertrude, the holy maiden of the Queen, was visited by "an Angel", who revealed to her a tale. The holy maiden was transformed by this revelation, and spread word of this miracle, and with it the worship of these creatures whom she considered "divine messengers". However, this "Angelic" faith was declared heretical in Lothric, since it was antithetical to the Way of White faith and undermined the legitimacy of Lothric's Firelinking duty. While Gertrude's faith went unrecognized by the Three Pillars that governed the realm, it nonetheless garnered a substantial body of followers within the Lothric army. This division seems to have erupted into a civil war amongst the army ranks, pitting the loyalists of the Pillars against the Winged Knights who followed Gertrude's Angelic Faith.

title: Londor
snippet: The Sable Church of Londor came to be seen as a haven for those with unsavory or blurry pasts, along with other rejects of the Age of Fire. The Church was physically identified by its black and twisted towers, a motif imitated in their artifacts. An increasing number of Undead and Hollows would find refuge in Londor, forming a society of wretchedly aged, deceitful, deeply detested Hollows. Their widespread stigmatization led the Hollows of Londor to adopt illusory rings which allowed them to retain a false human appearance. They also made use of purging stones that granted them some semblance of normalcy, which in some cases caused them to turn against their own kind.

snippet: Londor became host to a culture and religion that would be considered anathema by the Way of White faith. Liliane, as a founder of the Sable Church, weaved tales that portrayed the suffering and conflict of Hollows, to whom the Church aimed to bring salvation. These tales were recounted in dark miracle tomes which were forbidden in the rest of the world, on account of offering salvation to Hollows and conversely cursing all living beings. Londor espoused the veneration of the occult, and their tales/miracles were consequently focused on Hollows themselves, antithetical to the Way of White religion built around the gods of Anor Londo. The utility of the miracles derived from tales of Londor ranged from combative to cunning, and were accompanied by Velka's ancient miracles recovered by the Sable Church.

She is voiced by Jenny Funnel, who also voiced the Karla in the same game, Yuria and Selen Vinland in *Demon's Souls*, the Darkmoon Knightess and Quelana in *Dark Souls*, and Annalise and Iosefa in *Bloodborne*.

title: Old Woman of Londor
snippet:
Old Woman of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Her model is identical to that of Yoel of Londor.

title: Unkindled
snippet: The Unkindled are cursed with undeath, branded with the Darksign. Like their cursed undead predecessors, who obtained energy from fragments of the Dark Soul—Humanities in *Dark Souls* and Human Effigies in *Dark Souls II*—the Unkindled can benefit from the usage of Embers: scorched, consumed Humanities that are all that is left of the pure, original darkness at this late stage of the world. Finally, unlike previous *Dark Souls* protagonists, the Unkindled do not have to fear hollowing, as they can only achieve it willingly with the aid of Dark Sigils.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - plot 
 plot : By the times of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, the destined Lord of Cinder of his generation, has refused to link the First Flame. This led to the resurrection of four Lords of Cinder of the past, whose conjoined, withered embers could kindle the First Flame in Lothric's stead. Aldrich, Saint of the Deep; Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Ludleth of Courland were expected to sacrifice themselves as kindling once again. When all Lords except Ludleth rejected this duty, the Unkindled too were resurrected as a last resort, who were fated to seek out the Lords (including Prince Lothric) and bring them back to their thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once the cinders of the Lords were restored to their thrones, an Unkindled champion would be bestowed the embers of the First Flame that remained within their cinders, and finally sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to complete their journey.

title: Unkindled
snippet: The Sable Church of Londor revere the Unkindled, as it is prophesied that an Unkindled will become the Lord of Hollows and bring about the Age of Dark. Elfriede, the eldest of the three sisters of the Sable Church, eventually departed Londor and attempted to link the Flame. The circumstances surrounding her departure are unclear; whether she intended to usurp the Flame or wholly abandoned Londor is uncertain. Regardless, she was unable to link the Flame, burned to Unkindled Ash. After her resurrection, she was eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, a safe haven for the forlorn and the misshapen.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Hawkwood the Deserter, a former member of the Undead Legion of Farron who deserted during his first life. Hawkwood's connection to the Abyss Watchers, along with the time and details of his departure, are unclear; he does however demonstrate knowledge on the Undead Legion's induction rituals. He is noted for his crestfallen attitude, outwardly incredulous as to his duty as an Unkindled, and elects to remain at Firelink Shrine instead of pursuing his fate.
Horace the Hushed, who was the other child to have successfully escaped Aldrich, and travels alongside his sibling Anri. Although it is not stated outright that Horace is Unkindled, him still being naturally alive in *Dark Souls III* despite having first been born during Aldrich's era is unlikely, and the fact that he takes part in Anri's quest and appears in Firelink Shrine further point towards Horace being Unkindled like his sibling.

title: Unkindled
snippet: Unkindled resurrected to track down the Lords include the Ashen One, Anri of Astora, Horace the Hushed, Hawkwood the Deserter, and Siegward of Catarina. Some of these Unkindled are related to several of the respective Lords: Anri and Horace were children who survived Aldrich's gluttony, Siegward was an old friend of Yhorm's, and Hawkwood is a former member of the Abyss Watchers. Sister Friede is also Unkindled, although how and when she was brought back to life is unclear.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - lead 
 lead : The **Unkindled** or are "nameless, accursed Undead" who tried to link the First Flame and become Lords of Cinder, being mighty enough to reach the Kiln of the First Flame but ultimately perishing there, their quest ending in failure.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - unkindled_resurrected_to_supplant_lothric_younger_prince_prince_lothric 
 unkindled_resurrected_to_supplant_lothric_younger_prince_prince_lothric : The Ashen One, who eventually decides the fate of the First Flame.
Anri of Astora, who was one of only two children to have escaped the clutches of Aldrich, their cannibalistic father. Aldrich, as a Lord of Cinder, had been resurrected in the hopes of replacing Lothric; Anri in their second life aims to slay him, to fulfill their duty as a Lordseeker as well as to avenge their devoured siblings.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - other_known_unkindled 
 other_known_unkindled : Sister Friede, formerly known as **Elfriede**. It is unclear when she was resurrected and whether or not it happened in relation to Lothric. In her first life, she was the leader of the Sable Church of Londor, which aims to end the Age of Fire and bring about the Age of Dark; as such, she might have aimed to seize the First Flame rather than to link it. In her second life, Elfriede, now renamed Friede, renounced her past, instead making a home in the Painted World of Ariandel.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: "Drawing Out True Strength" five times is necessary to complete Yoel's questline, which, together with the subsequent Yuria of Londor questline, lead to The Usurpation of Fire ending. It must be done before reaching the Catacombs of Carthus, since if Yoel is still alive when the player reaches said location, he will die the very moment the Catacombs are entered (including in the Settlement if he has not been recruited). If Yoel dies without having "Drawn Out True Strength" five times, or if the player heals their Dark Sigils with the Fire Keeper after she receives the Fire Keeper Soul, the Londor questline will have failed.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - questline 
 questline : Yoel is first encountered near the beginning of the Undead Settlement, at the edge of a crumbled bridge. The only survivor among many other less fortunate pilgrims like him, he seems enlightened to be in the presence of the Ashen One and asks if he could be allowed in their service. Agreeing to his plea will make him move to Firelink Shrine. There, he can be found on the lowermost level, at the end of the right corridor past Greirat, where he will sell an assortment of Sorceries to the player. Refusing his service will result in Yoel remaining in this spot, waiting for the Ashen One to change their mind.

Selecting the "Talk" option while in his interaction menu will teach the player the "Beckon" gesture. As a former sorcerer, all of his wares are sorceries.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Selecting the "Talk" option while in his interaction menu will teach the player the "Beckon" gesture. As a former sorcerer, all of his wares are sorceries.

Yoel also offers to level up the Ashen One without the use of souls. By selecting the "Draw Out True Strength" option, he will do so, functioning much like the Fire Keeper. Leveling up this way will place a Dark Sigil in the player's inventory. From this point onward, every time the player dies, they will gain a Hollowing level based on the number of Dark Sigils they possess. At 2, 6, 12 and 15 Hollowing, Yoel will again present the player with the option to level up for free, granting them an additional Dark Sigil each time up to a maximum of 5.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : He is first encountered near the Foot of the High Wall bonfire in the Undead Settlement, on the other end of the bridge from the gate leading into the settlement proper. The area is filled with dead pilgrims, although Yoel, located to the right, is still alive and can be talked to. He will offer to enter into Ashen One's service, and if the player accepts will move to Firelink Shrine. He can be found in the basement, at the end of the corridor on the west wing.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Upon reaching the Catacombs of Carthus, Yoel will die and his services will no longer be available, ending his questline prematurely unless the player has gotten all five Dark Sigils from him.
**Yoel dies exactly the moment the "Catacombs of Carthus" banner appears on the screen, so it is perfectly safe to fight the Abyss Watchers beforehand and use the bonfire that appears after the battle, as long as the player does not descend the staircase that opens in that room. If you don't level up with him at all before he dies, it will cause the failure of Yuria's questline and the Londor Pale Shade to invade at two different points of the game.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Yoel of Londor** is a character and merchant in *Dark Souls III*. He is voiced by David Sterne.

A gentle, soft-spoken pilgrim of Londor who relocates to Firelink Shrine after being met in the Undead Settlement, he offers the Ashen One his wares as sorcerer as well as a unique, "free" way to level up in souls up to five times. Doing so prior to reaching the Catacombs of Carthus is a requirement for the Londor questline (see The Usurpation of Fire ending).

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
Yoel of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Yoel is a former sorcerer from Londor. Although he feels that the sorceries of Londor pale in comparison with those of Vinheim, he knows how to use his skills to draw out strength from humans. One of the pilgrims of Londor whose nature is unclear and travel to Lothric on a quest meant to culminate in death, Yoel failed in his mission, as he lives still among the bodies of his more successful comrades, until the appearance of the Ashen One offers him an unexpected chance for redemption.

He was a friend and follower of Yuria of Londor, one of the three founders of the Sable Church of Londor.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: **The nature of the Pilgrims of Londor, and what the death they seek means to them, are left unexplained, but it is worth noting that if the player makes Yuria hostile, she claims that "Yoel knows not of thy folly," speaking of him in the present tense even though he will always have died by the time she appears.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet: Yoel's dead body will be on the same spot he was when the Ashen One last saw him; uncharacteristically, his dead body will always remain, unless the player killed him themselves. If his questline was completed, Yuria will be next to his body, selling his old wares and allowing for the questline to continue. It is of note that killing Yoel after obtaining all five Dark Sigils does not void the questline, although there are no benefits to doing so.

title: Yoel of Londor
snippet:
He was a friend and follower of Yuria of Londor, one of the three founders of the Sable Church of Londor.

Upon appearing following Yoel's questline and his death, Yuria claims to be "a close friend of [Yoel]" and will declare that thanks to the Ashen One, Yoel has redeemed himself. Yoel' dying words if he is killed before completing his questline confirm that he did know Yuria, and if he is killed after completing his questline (meaning five Dark Sigils have been obtained) he will gleefully thank the Ashen One for this death, confirming that whatever manner he may die to within Firelink Shrine while the Ashen One is away, he is very likely willing.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - description 
 description : Having three founders of the Black Church ensured Yuria's legacy would survive. Her two sisters could carry the torch, making certain their lord claims the flame, for the sake of all Hollows.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - notes 
 notes : Yuria will leave Firelink Shrine if the player talks to her after healing their accumulated Dark Sigil. If the player does not engage in dialogue with her after healing their Dark Sigils, Yuria will remain in Firelink Shrine indefinitely, though this serves no practical purpose.
Yuria only drops her ashes if the player kills her. As such, defeating the Soul of Cinder will mean that her wares are no longer available, unless she is killed before she has a chance to leave.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - ashes_of_ariandel 
 ashes_of_ariandel : Yuria possesses additional dialogue should the player progress through the Painted World of Ariandel. After talking to Sister Friede and returning to Firelink Shrine, Yuria will recognize the scent of her sister, and warn the Ashen One of heeding their kindness over their principles.

Once Sister Friede has been defeated and the player is in possession of her soul, Yuria will remark on Elfriede's history with Londor, and request that the Ashen One usurp the First Flame in her memory.

Should the player have not yet acquired 8 Dark Sigils in either case, the dialogue will vary slightly.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - base_game 
 base_game : Upon introducing herself, Yuria reveals that Yoel was a close friend to her and thanks the Champion of Ash for allowing him to be redeemed through his actions while at their service. She then does the same, pledging allegiance to the player and accepting them as her Lord and of all the hollows in Londor, in the hope that one day the Ashen One brings back its glory to the world.

Upon talking to her, the player will learn the "Dignified Bow" gesture.

Once Orbeck of Vinheim has moved to Firelink Shrine, Yuria will alert the player that he has proclaimed himself to be "Lord of Hollows," asking the player to settle the matter lest he imperil the player's rule. If the player brings Orbeck's Ashes to Yuria, she will reward them with the Morion Blade.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Found in Firelink Shrine, at the end of the corridor on the west wing of the basement, in the same area where Yoel of Londor is found.

In order for Yuria to appear, the player must draw out their true strength (level up) with Yoel and acquire all five Dark Sigils before reaching the Catacombs of Carthus. The next time the player visits Yoel's usual place in Firelink Shrine, they will find him already dead with Yuria standing close by.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet: Once the player reaches the Catacombs of Carthus, Yuria reveals that she is also guiding Anri of Astora along the path to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, and plans to engage him/her (gender is always the opposite of the player's) in matrimony. To this end, the player must aid Anri and keep him/her alive up until Pontiff Sulyvahn has been defeated (care must be taken not to kill the Londor Pilgrim within the Church of Yorshka). If successful, Anri may be found in the old Darkmoon tomb, Dark Sun Gwyndolin's boss arena in *Dark Souls*, and can be "married" here, gaining 3 more Dark Sigils for a total of 8.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Yuria of Londor** is a character and merchant in *Dark Souls III*. She is a mentor of the Sable Church and accomplished swordswoman, said to have claimed a hundred lives with her sword, the Darkdrift.

She is voiced by Pooky Quesnel, who also voiced Arianna in *Bloodborne*.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Once the player completes their wedding vows, Yuria will swear her fealty to the true Lord of Hollows. She will no longer become aggressive if attacked by the player, short of the Dark Sigils being healed by the Fire Keeper. She will also make herself available to be summoned for the Soul of Cinder fight. Should she be summoned and survive this fight, her set and weapon can be found at her usual spot at Firelink Shrine.

If Yoel dies before the player can attain all five Dark Sigils, Yuria will not appear and the Londor Pale Shade will invade in the Farron Keep and Irithyll of the Boreal Valley; the Pale Shade will also invade the player at these locations should Yuria be killed or angered. Defeating the Pale Shade once will reward the Manikin Claws, while defeating them at both locations will cause the Pale Shade Set to appear at Firelink Shrine in the same area where Yuria and Yoel used to reside.

title: Yuria of Londor
snippet:
Yuria of Londor -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Yuria's line upon death: "Kaathe... I have failed thee" can be better translated as "Kaathe... Your dying wish was unfulfilled", implying that the Primordial Serpent died of unknown causes before the events of *Dark Souls III*.
Yuria's armor set, in particular the helmet, is based on the Cainhurst Set from *Bloodborne*. Additionally, the Cainhurst Vilebloods also used katanas.
Yuria shares her name with Yuria the Witch, a character from *Demon's Souls*.
**Yuria and Yuliya are names commonly used in Miyazaki directed games, minus Sekiro.
Yuria wields Darkdrift, a katana originally from *Dark Souls II*. It too belonged to an NPC that delved in the shadows and spoke for Hollows.
Like Oswald of Carim from *Dark Souls*, she wears an armor set called the "Black Set" and she sells Velka Miracles in the Londor Braille Divine Tome, Purging Stones, and Rings of Sacrifice.
